title: himorime benchmark suite
description: A versioned himorime benchmark suite. See https://nao1215.github.io/himorime/configuration/.

warmup.description: Unmeasured runs of every command before measuring starts. Default 1.

runs.description: Measure exactly this many runs per command. When absent, runs are adaptive: at least min_runs and min_time, at most max_runs.

min_runs.description: Adaptive runs: the fewest runs per command. Default 10.

max_runs.description: Adaptive runs: the most runs per command. Default 100.

min_time.description: Adaptive runs: keep measuring until each command has run for at least this long in total. Default 2s.

timeout.description: Per-run time limit. A run that exceeds it is stopped with its whole process tree and fails the benchmark. Default 1m.

cwd.description: Working directory: relative to ${root} (the suite directory in the revision being measured), or starting with ${root}, ${head_root} or ${workdir}. Default: ${root}, so each revision runs its own files.

env.description: Environment variables added to the inherited environment. Values may use variables.

stdout.description: "discard" (default), or a path inside ${workdir} that receives the standard output of the latest run.

stderr.description: "discard" (default), or a path inside ${workdir} that receives the standard error of the latest run. A failing run's stderr tail is reported either way.

exit_codes.description: Exit statuses that count as success. Default [0].

build.description: Builds ${artifact} before measuring; in a comparison it runs once in each revision, with ${root} pointing into that revision.

report.description: Report files written after every run, relative to the suite file.

section.description: Markdown only: replace the section of this name in the existing file, between its himorime:begin and himorime:end comment lines, and keep the rest of the file. Lowercase letters, digits and '-'.

versions.description: Tools whose versions every report records, such as jc: [jc, --version]. Each command runs once in the suite directory before measuring, with a 30s time limit; the first non-empty line it prints is recorded, and a failure fails the run.

duration.description: A duration such as 500ms, 2s or 1m30s. Units: ns, us, µs, ms, s, m, h.

budget.description: An upper bound on a duration: < or <= followed by a duration greater than zero, such as "< 20ms".

bytesBudget.description: An upper bound on a byte size: < or <= followed by a size greater than zero, such as "<= 64MiB". KB, MB, GB and TB are powers of 1000; KiB, MiB, GiB and TiB powers of 1024.

rateBudget.description: A lower bound on throughput: > or >= followed by a rate greater than zero in the declared work unit per second, such as ">= 50MiB/s" or ">= 1000 records/s".

percentBudget.description: A bound on a percentage in either direction, such as "<= 150%".

rate.description: A rate in the declared work unit per second, such as 1MiB/s or "100 records/s".

durationBudgets.description: Budgets of a duration keyed by aggregation: min, max, mean, median, or a percentile p1 to p99.9 such as p95.

bytesBudgets.description: Budgets of a byte size keyed by aggregation: min, max, mean, median, or a percentile p1 to p99.9 such as p95.

rateBudgets.description: Budgets of throughput keyed by aggregation: min, max, mean, median, or a percentile p1 to p99.9 such as p95.

percentBudgets.description: Budgets of a percentage keyed by aggregation: min, max, mean, median, or a percentile p1 to p99.9 such as p95.

percent.description: A percentage greater than 0 and at most 1000.

pathTemplate.description: A relative path, which is relative to ${root}, or a path starting with ${root}, ${head_root} or ${workdir}. Absolute paths and '..' after a variable are rejected.

relativePath.description: A relative path that stays below its base directory.

exitCodes.description: Exit statuses that count as success.

command.description: A list of arguments, or a string used with shell: true.

versionCommand.description: A list of arguments whose first element is the program; no shell.

shellRule.description: A string command requires shell: true; shell: true requires a string command.

exec.description: A process himorime starts: the build or a hook. `command` is a list of arguments run without a shell, or a string together with `shell: true`.

command.description: The command: a list of arguments (no shell), or a string when shell is true.

shell.description: Run the command string through /bin/sh -c (cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). Variables substituted into the string are quoted for that shell.

cwd.description: Working directory: relative to ${root} of the revision being built or measured (the default), or starting with ${root}, ${head_root}, or ${workdir} in hooks.

env.description: Environment variables added to the inherited environment. Values may use variables.

timeout.description: Time limit for this process. Default 10m for build, 5m for hooks.

benchCommand.description: One named command of a benchmark.

command.description: The command: a list of arguments (no shell), or a string when shell is true.

shell.description: Run the command string through /bin/sh -c (cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). Variables substituted into the string are quoted for that shell.

cwd.description: Working directory: relative to ${root} (the suite directory in the revision being measured), or starting with ${root}, ${head_root} or ${workdir}. Default: ${root}, so each revision runs its own files.

env.description: Environment variables added to the inherited environment. Values may use variables.

timeout.description: Per-run time limit. A run that exceeds it is stopped with its whole process tree and fails the benchmark. Default 1m.

stdout.description: "discard" (default), or a path inside ${workdir} that receives the standard output of the latest run.

stderr.description: "discard" (default), or a path inside ${workdir} that receives the standard error of the latest run. A failing run's stderr tail is reported either way.

exit_codes.description: Exit statuses that count as success. Default [0].

latency.description: Latency budgets keyed by aggregation, such as {p95: "<= 100ms"}.

throughput.description: Throughput budgets keyed by aggregation. Needs metrics.throughput.work.

cpu_user.description: User CPU time budgets keyed by aggregation. Needs metrics.cpu.

cpu_system.description: System CPU time budgets keyed by aggregation. Needs metrics.cpu.

cpu_total.description: Total (user + system) CPU time budgets keyed by aggregation. Needs metrics.cpu.

cpu_utilization.description: CPU utilization budgets keyed by aggregation, in percent of one CPU; above 100% means more than one CPU was busy. Needs metrics.cpu.

peak_rss.description: Peak resident set size budgets keyed by aggregation. Needs metrics.memory.

regression.description: How a base revision and the working tree are compared (himorime compare / himorime ci).

confidence.description: Bootstrap probability required to call a regression, an improvement or a pass. Default 0.95.

min_samples.description: Fewest samples per side for a verdict. In a comparison, adaptive runs keep measuring until every compared command has this many; fewer is inconclusive. Default 10.

max_cv.description: Overlapping or touching sample ranges are inconclusive when either side exceeds this dispersion: IQR / 1.349 / median, or standard deviation / mean for the mean. Completely separated ranges still need the sample count, tolerance and bootstrap confidence checks. 0 disables the noise check. Default 0.5.

regressionBenchmark.description: How a base revision and the working tree are compared (himorime compare / himorime ci).

confidence.description: Bootstrap probability required to call a regression, an improvement or a pass. Default 0.95.

min_samples.description: Fewest samples per side for a verdict. In a comparison, adaptive runs keep measuring until every compared command has this many; fewer is inconclusive. Default 10.

max_cv.description: Overlapping or touching sample ranges are inconclusive when either side exceeds this dispersion: IQR / 1.349 / median, or standard deviation / mean for the mean. Completely separated ranges still need the sample count, tolerance and bootstrap confidence checks. 0 disables the noise check. Default 0.5.

commands.description: Compare only these commands. Default: every command.

name.description: Unique benchmark name shown in reports.

warmup.description: Unmeasured runs of every command before measuring starts. Default 1.

runs.description: Measure exactly this many runs per command. When absent, runs are adaptive: at least min_runs and min_time, at most max_runs.

min_runs.description: Adaptive runs: the fewest runs per command. Default 10.

max_runs.description: Adaptive runs: the most runs per command. Default 100.

min_time.description: Adaptive runs: keep measuring until each command has run for at least this long in total. Default 2s.

timeout.description: Per-run time limit. A run that exceeds it is stopped with its whole process tree and fails the benchmark. Default 1m.

cwd.description: Working directory: relative to ${root} (the suite directory in the revision being measured), or starting with ${root}, ${head_root} or ${workdir}. Default: ${root}, so each revision runs its own files.

env.description: Environment variables added to the inherited environment. Values may use variables.

stdout.description: "discard" (default), or a path inside ${workdir} that receives the standard output of the latest run.

stderr.description: "discard" (default), or a path inside ${workdir} that receives the standard error of the latest run. A failing run's stderr tail is reported either way.

exit_codes.description: Exit statuses that count as success. Default [0].

stdin.description: Standard input of every run: a fixture path (reopened for each run), or a mapping with file or content.

oneOf.description: Fixture path: relative to ${root} of the revision being measured, or starting with ${root}, ${head_root} or ${workdir}. Use ${head_root} to give every revision the working tree's file.

file.description: Fixture path, as in the string form.

content.description: Inline text passed on standard input.

terminal.description: Run every command on a pseudo-terminal of 80 columns and 24 rows (Linux and macOS): standard input, output and error are the terminal, stdin is typed into it one key at a time once the command is ready and has read the key before, and what the command writes goes to stdout. The input must end the program. stderr cannot be set.

setup.description: Processes run once per benchmark (per revision in a comparison) before any warmup. A failure fails the benchmark.

prepare_each.description: Processes run before every warmup and measured run, outside the measured time.

cleanup.description: Processes run after the benchmark whether it passed, failed or was interrupted.

baseline.description: Command name that RELATIVE and vs_baseline are computed against.

commands.description: Named commands measured side by side. Names use letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'.

work.description: The work one run does. Throughput is this work divided by the run's latency. Declare exactly one of value and file_size.

value.description: A fixed amount of work per run, greater than zero, such as 100000.

file_size.description: A file whose size in bytes is the work of each run: relative to ${root} of the revision being measured, or starting with ${root}, ${head_root} or ${workdir}. Read before every run, outside the measured time.

unit.description: The unit of work, such as records, lines or bytes. Default: operations for value, bytes for file_size.

metricsDefaults.description: Metrics every benchmark measures besides latency. Throughput is declared per benchmark.

cpu.description: Measure user, system and total CPU time and CPU utilization of the process tree.

memory.description: Measure the peak resident set size (RSS) of the process tree.

unsupported.description: What to do when this platform cannot measure a requested metric: fail (default) stops before measuring, skip reports the metric as unsupported and skips its budgets and comparisons.

metrics.description: What the benchmark measures besides latency.

cpu.description: Measure user, system and total CPU time and CPU utilization of the process tree.

memory.description: Measure the peak resident set size (RSS) of the process tree.

unsupported.description: What to do when this platform cannot measure a requested metric: fail (default) stops before measuring, skip reports the metric as unsupported and skips its budgets and comparisons.

latencyRegression.description: How latency (wall-clock time; lower is better) is compared.

max_percent.description: Tolerated degradation in percent: a number such as 10, or a string such as "10%". Default 10.

min_difference.description: The smallest absolute difference that can be a regression or an improvement; smaller differences pass. A duration such as 1ms for latency and cpu, a byte size such as 1MiB for memory. Default: none.

gate.description: Whether this metric's verdict decides the result and the exit status (default true). With false the metric is still compared and reported, marked as not gated, but a regression or an inconclusive result never fails the run.

cpuRegression.description: How total CPU time (lower is better) is compared.

min_difference.description: The smallest absolute difference that can be a regression or an improvement, such as 1ms. Default: none.

gate.description: Whether this metric's verdict decides the result and the exit status (default true). With false the metric is still compared and reported, marked as not gated, but a regression or an inconclusive result never fails the run.

memoryRegression.description: How peak RSS (lower is better) is compared.

max_percent.description: Tolerated degradation in percent: a number such as 10, or a string such as "10%". Default 10.

min_difference.description: The smallest absolute difference that can be a regression or an improvement, such as 1MiB. Default: none.
